fatal_errors: The proposed comparison omits the central as-printed versus 750°C/50 h precipitation-aged states and their L12/L21 precipitates.
It replaces the relevant baseline with an unspecified conventional alloy, confounding alloy composition with oxide-scale stability.
It does not identify the continuous Cr2O3 layer, Cr redistribution, precipitate-associated Cr depletion, or matrix–precipitate interfaces as the governing mechanisms.
The asserted 10–50 nm scale thickness and 30% oxidation-rate and 25% integrity improvements are unsupported and inconsistent with the supplied evidence.
The proposed oxygen-pressure range is invented; the atmosphere in the target study was not explicitly reported.
In-situ TEM and APT do not reproduce the target bulk isothermal oxidation protocol or its principal kinetic and cross-sectional measurements.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad idea that a stable oxide barrier can control high-temperature oxidation, but it remains generic and does not reconstruct the study's testable mechanism. The target concerns an SLM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy, aging-induced L12/L21 precipitation, and delayed formation of a protective continuous Cr-rich scale caused by Cr-depleted precipitates and added interfaces. The generated hypothesis instead compares unspecified alloys with and without an assumed nanoscale oxide, so composition, processing, and scale stability are all confounded. Its temperature window overlaps only part of the 600–1200°C range, and it misses the 96 h kinetics, subparabolic-to-near-parabolic behavior, duplex/trilayer scale, and similar activation energies of the two states. Although the falsification thresholds are explicit, they are arbitrary and unsupported by cited evidence, making the experiment weakly discriminating and the overall hypothesis unsupported.
